elements.text: the training, validation and testing data sets of a high-risk AI system
the data sets used for development meet defined quality criteria
the quality criteria are those of Article 10(2) to 10(5) (governance, representativeness, statistical properties, context of use, special-category safeguards)
training, validation and testing data sets
the data sets are subject to data governance and management practices
the practices are appropriate for the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system
data governance and management practices address the relevant design choices
design choices of the high-risk AI system that bear on its data (not only the format of the data set)
data governance practices address the data collection processes
the origin (provenance) of the data is recorded and governed
for personal data, the original purpose of the data collection is identified
data governance practices address data-preparation processing operations
the operations covered include annotation and labelling
the operations covered include cleaning, updating, enrichment and aggregation
assumptions about the data are explicitly formulated
the assumptions concern the information the data is supposed to measure and represent
an assessment of the data sets that are needed is carried out
the assessment covers availability, quantity and suitability of the needed data sets
the data sets are examined for possible biases
the examination targets biases likely to affect the health and safety of persons or to have a negative impact on fundamental rights
the examination targets biases that could lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law
the examination pays particular attention where outputs influence inputs for future operations (feedback loops)
data gaps or shortcomings are identified
the gaps or shortcomings are those that prevent compliance with the Regulation
it is determined how the gaps and shortcomings can be addressed
the data sets are relevant and sufficiently representative
the data sets are, to the best extent possible, free of errors and complete
these properties are judged in view of the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system
the data sets have appropriate statistical properties
the statistical properties are appropriate as regards the persons or groups of persons on whom the system is intended to be used
the data sets take into account characteristics of the setting of intended use
the characteristics are specific to the geographical, contextual, behavioural or functional setting
the extent is that required by the intended purpose
special categories of personal data (GDPR Art. 9(1))
special-category personal data is processed for the purpose of bias detection and correction
the processing is strictly necessary and exceptional
appropriate safeguards for the fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons apply
it is established that bias detection and correction cannot be effectively fulfilled by processing other data
the alternatives considered include synthetic or anonymised data
special categories of personal data used for bias detection
technical limitations on the re-use of the personal data are applied
state-of-the-art security and privacy-preserving measures, including pseudonymisation, are applied
special categories of personal data used for bias detection
the personal data is deleted
deletion occurs once the bias has been corrected or the personal data has reached the end of its retention period, whichever comes first
the high-risk AI system is not developed using techniques involving the training of AI models
the data quality obligations of paragraphs 2 to 5 are applied to the testing data sets
